check.summary: Candidate a4a44bf6 (parent 79414143, tree 2c123d9f) changes exactly two paths: one JSX text node in SupportView.tsx (line 195) and +95/-3 in support-documents.test.tsx; no server, shared, api.ts, dependency, route, payment or protection-manifest path moves. Reasoned from source, the outcome==="error" branch is reached in production only through accountPortalFetch returning {kind:"error"}, which it does for a transport rejection, for any non-envelope/unparseable body on a non-401/403 status (including 201 with a lost body and proxy pages), and for a server 500 envelope that guarded() emits only after the handler threw, where the Supabase insert().select().single() chain can already have persisted the row. Every definitive refusal (400 invalid_support_case, 429 rate_limited, 401/403 guard or wall denials) arrives as a denied envelope or a 401/403 status and renders the unchanged denied/rate_limited copy that still says "Your request was not recorded"; the dead ungraduated fallback is not wired in production. The new copy is therefore truthful on every path that reaches it and is strictly more conservative than the base copy, which asserted non-recording for the same uncertain paths. Draft (category, subject, description) is retained on error/denied/rate_limited and cleared only on ok, unchanged from base. The tests discriminate: the three new/rewritten error cases assert the alert text equals the new copy and reject the base wording, so they fail at 79414143; the it.each pair drives the real createAccountSupportCase/accountPortalFetch with a stubbed global fetch (transport throw; 201 Response with json() rejecting), asserts one POST to /api/research/customer-account/support with the trimmed body, no retry, draft retained, prior case retained, no status element, and raw error strings not rendered. No .only/.skip/.todo; result.json reports 13/13 passed, 0 pending, 0 todo. The receipt binds candidate and tree to the frozen clean HEAD via the launcher, pins the Node binary, root lock and installed-metadata hashes, matches argv and 13 names in run.log; blob ids and byte sizes for the records files match the registration. Named limits: synthetic jsdom evidence only, no browser, backend, idempotency, build or typecheck; node_modules identity rests on lock/metadata hashes with no full-tree digest; sha256 values were not independently recomputed. One P2 (case-history list is a mount-time snapshot, so the copy directs the customer to a list that cannot show the possibly-recorded case until a reload) and three P3 notes; none require correction before acceptance.

findings.title: Copy directs the customer to a case list that is a mount-time snapshot and will not show the possibly-recorded case until reload
findings.claim: "Check your case history before submitting again" points at the same page's "Your cases" section, but that list is loaded once per (loader, token) identity and nothing refetches after an error outcome, so a case that was persisted during the lost exchange stays invisible until the customer reloads or navigates away and back; a customer who checks the stale list and resubmits creates the duplicate the copy is trying to prevent. Not a regression: the base copy asserted non-recording and invited an immediate resubmit on the same paths.
findings.evidence: SupportView.tsx:195 and :209-228@a4a44bf6 (list = createdCases + cases prop; createdCases only grows on ok at 109); AccountSupport.tsx:9,17@a4a44bf6 (cases from useAccountResource(loadAccountSupport, memberToken), onSubmit does not touch the resource); resource.tsx:64-95@a4a44bf6 (effect keyed on request identity only; no refetch API exposed); SupportView.tsx:227 caveat "Case-history completeness is not reported here"; SOURCE_AND_TEST_RESULT.json defect note "no claim that currently loaded history is fresh or complete".
findings.fix: In a follow-up slice (not required for this acceptance): after setOutcome("error"), trigger a reload of loadAccountSupport (e.g. a refresh token/dependency passed into useAccountResource, or a page-level reload callback) and merge the fresh list, or at minimum word the copy "reload this page and check your case history before submitting again" and add a test that the list shows a server-visible new case after an uncertain outcome.

The sentence remains literally true (the client cannot confirm), it is strictly better than the base copy for the uncertain paths, and each of these conditions also fails the GET /support load through the same guard so AccountResourceBoundary shows its error state and SupportView never mounts. Named for completeness of the 'definitive refusal mislabelled as uncertain' hunt; not a defect requiring correction.

missed.title: Pre-existing cause misattribution in two definitive refusals, unchanged here
missed.claim: (a) accountSupportSubmissionAllowed uses durableFailurePolicy 'deny', so when the durable rate-limit RPC is unavailable or errors the write is refused as 'support_rate_limited' and the customer reads 'Too many support requests were submitted recently' although they submitted nothing recently. verify.opinion: Accept with the named limits. I tried to break the candidate in the four ways the brief asked for and could not. There is no definitive-refusal path that the new copy turns into a false statement: every server-authored refusal (400, 429, 401, 403) still renders the unchanged 'not recorded' copies, and the only inputs that reach line 195 are transport loss, non-envelope bodies, and the post-openCase 500, exactly the cases where the base copy was lying. Draft and category survive every non-ok branch, and the diff is a single text node, so no state, handler or validation moved. The four rewritten error tests fail at 79414143 on an exact-text assertion plus a negative regex, and the it.each pair really does exercise accountPortalFetch with only fetch stubbed, one POST, no retry. The receipt binds the candidate SHA and tree through a launcher that refuses a dirty or mismatched HEAD, and its timestamps, counts and test names reconcile across receipt.json, result.json and run.log to within seconds and milliseconds. The genuine weakness is the one the checker already named as AS-1: the copy sends the customer to a list that is a mount-time snapshot, and (ASV-1) the notice itself vanishes on the first keystroke, so the duplicate guard is advisory. Relative to base that is still a strict improvement, which is why it stays P2 and not P1. What this acceptance does not say: nothing here is browser, backend, idempotency, build, typecheck or protection evidence; the dependency tree is a donor copy identified by two hashes; and no sha256 was recomputed in this review.
deviations: Seven `git show` outputs were piped through `cat -n` for line numbering; `cat -n` is a read-only pipe target not in the enumerated grep/sed -n/head/wc list. No file outside the two allowed directories was read directly and nothing was created, modified, executed or deleted.
`git log` was invoked with `--format` and `git diff` with `--stat`; both are enumerated subcommands (log, diff) run read-only against C:/xenios-wt/health-review with --no-optional-locks.
One `git grep` output was piped through `grep -v` before `head`; both are allowed targets.

No other deviations: Read/Grep/Glob were used only on the review records directory and the scratch ql/ directory; no cd, echo, variables, loops, redirection or command chaining; no interpreter, test run, MCP, WebFetch, checkout/fetch/commit/push, or session contact; sha256 values were not recomputed because no hashing command is in the allowed set.
